root_cause.text: In `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()`, when a failure occurs after the access_pattern subdirectories have been created, the error cleanup path fails to call `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs()` to remove those subdirectories, leaving stale sysfs entries and causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern)` in the new label `rmdir_put_access_pattern_out` before the existing `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj)`. The original code only performed `kobject_put` under `put_access_pattern_out` without removing the subdirectories, which were created by a prior call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()`.

The original code only performed `kobject_put` under `put_access_pattern_out` without removing the subdirectories, which were created by a prior call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_add_dirs()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling in damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs to properly clean up the access pattern sysfs directory when setting destinations fails.
intent_record.what: Changed the goto target in error handling of damos_sysfs_set_dests from 'put_access_pattern_out' to 'rmdir_put_access_pattern_out'.
intent_record.how: When damos_sysfs_set_dests fails, the code now jumps to a label that first removes (rmdir) the access pattern sysfs directory before putting (decrementing refcount) the object, ensuring proper cleanup of the previously created directory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing cleanup of access pattern sysfs directories in error path of damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs.
intent_record.what: Added a new label 'rmdir_put_access_pattern_out' and inserted a call to damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs before kobject_put and NULL assignment in the error handling path of damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs.
intent_record.how: When an error occurs during scheme directory addition, the access pattern sysfs directories are now explicitly removed before releasing the kobject reference, ensuring proper cleanup and preventing resource leaks.
